inputs.text: An Indiana judge has blocked an abortion restriction after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it would interfere with people’s sincerely held religious beliefs. That matters, but the deeper issue is the state using its power to control private decisions about bodies and belief. These restrictions don’t affect everyone equally: people with fewer resources have the least ability to absorb the barriers. Religious freedom and reproductive autonomy both demand that access to care not be dictated by the state or reserved for those who can afford to navigate its restrictions.
